subject: English Literature
unit: Spring 2: Masterclass and Component 1: anthology, unseen poetry and Of Mice and Men
source: Seeded from english-literature/y11 lesson 36 (Masterclass question sheet (teacher-written, pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 36: Masterclass: the conceptual thesis and the analytical paragraph in every Literature answer. Answer every question. Show your working. Mark it with the mark scheme and log any errors in your repair list.

questions.q: in the portal response box, write a thesis and one analytical paragraph for your weakest component (question on the pupil PDF). Starter: '[Writer] presents...'
questions.a: A conceptual thesis and a paragraph with argument, short evidence, method, zoom, effect and the right AO (context or comparison).
questions.model: Macbeth: 'Shakespeare presents Lady Macbeth's collapse as the return of buried guilt. "Out, damned spot!" turns the "little water" of Act 2 into an endless stain; the imperative "Out" shows she can no longer command even herself, which a Jacobean audience would read as divine justice.'

questions.q: label each part of your paragraph.
add personal engagement: one sentence of your own judgement.
questions.a: For example: I find her collapse more disturbing than Macbeth's death, because it is so quiet.

questions.q: Write conceptual theses for two questions on the pupil PDF (one per component).
questions.a: Two conceptual theses naming the writer and a big idea.
questions.model: Question: 'How does Priestley present Sheila?' Thesis: 'Priestley presents Sheila as the hope of the younger generation: her change from privileged daughter to moral voice shows that people can learn responsibility.'

questions.q: Answer the ponder in one sentence.
questions.a: Knowing is plot and quotations; having something to say is an argument about meaning.
